summary: Adobe's identity page asks for the email, then for the password, in one single-page document on auth.services.adobe.com. This repository already has a reviewed adapter for that document, written for the adobe-admin-console profile. No steps file: the two stages differ only by URL fragment, which the format cannot gate on.

sources.title: The reviewed Adobe staged sign-in adapter
sources.note: Lines 71-80: only /en_US/index.html with the fragment #/ (email) or #/password is accepted. Lines 137-150: the two forms, their fields and buttons. Lines 151-153 and 164-170: the password stage must carry a hidden read-only username field equal to the email just typed.

sources.title: The synthetic email and password forms the adapter is tested against
sources.note: Lines 170-184 show the adapter refusing other documents and fragments: /fr_FR/index.html, #/signup, #/identities, #/challenge, #/federated-wait, #/login/code, #/welcome-back.

sources.title: Adobe route catalog: the login origins approved for adobe-admin-console
sources.note: Lists adobe-admin-console only; account.adobe.com is not in it.

sources.title: Hosted dashboard profiles: the reviewed Adobe flow and its limits
sources.note: Line 210: reviewed English email-then-password flow at auth.services.adobe.com/en_US/index.html from #/ to #/password, and the Adobe Account (adobe) preset remains manual-only.

selectors.note: The hidden read-only field that repeats the account. The adapter types the password only while its value equals the email it typed.

fixtures.note: The email stage, shown with the fragment #/.
The password stage of the same document, shown with the fragment #/password.

staysInteractive.note: Federated and enterprise identities leave the reviewed document.
One-time codes and other verification (#/challenge, #/login/code), sign-up and recovery routes, and every locale other than en_US: the adapter stops on all of them.

unverified: That https://account.adobe.com/ sends a signed-out visitor to https://auth.services.adobe.com/en_US/index.html. The repository reviewed that document for adobe-admin-console; nothing read here shows where Adobe Account lands, and no capture of account.adobe.com was made.
The live page as served today: the adapter's tests use synthetic forms, and docs/hosted-dashboard-profiles.md line 206 says no authenticated sign-in has been completed.
Other locales, regions and experiments; the adapter accepts the en_US document only.
neededFromUser: The address the browser shows after opening https://account.adobe.com/ signed out, or that page saved as "Webpage, Complete". It settles whether Adobe Account uses the reviewed document; one sign-in settles the rest. Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
schemaGaps: URL fragment gates. The email and password stages are the same document, /en_US/index.html, told apart only by the fragment (#/ and #/password), and the adapter refuses every other fragment such as #/signup, #/identities and #/challenge. A step's path gate sees the pathname only.
The password stage is bound to the account: the adapter types the password only when the hidden read-only username field holds the email it typed. A step cannot state that.
notes: No steps file: Adobe keeps its dedicated adapter (catalog loginFlow adobe). The catalog gives this profile no loginFlow and adobeHostedRoutes.json lists adobe-admin-console only, so reusing the adapter for account.adobe.com is catalog and route work; mechanism is form because the corpus check accepts adapter only for a profile that has a loginFlow. No capture: Adobe's General Terms of Use, section 6.18, bar data gathering and extraction methods, and the coordinator decided against one.
